title: The Economist: ownership and control
summary: The Economist is a British international news publication. Exor holds 43.4% of its publisher. Stephen Smith and his investment interests acquired a combined 26.95% in April 2026. Shareholder voting is capped, while special shareholders and trustees hold separate appointment rights.

gaps: Research cutoff: 2026-09-18. Findings are unreviewed; undated ownership pages have null observation dates.

The Smith acquisition is reported as 26.9% in the completion release and 26.95% in the annual report. The split between Stephen Smith personally and SFC International Holdings Limited was not established.

Companies House dates the new significant-shareholder entry to 2026-04-20; the publisher states completion occurred on 2026-04-23. Stephen Smith's ceased personal PSC entry does not establish that he ceased holding a smaller personal stake.

The acquisition announcement names Smith Financial Corporation, whereas the register identifies SFC International Holdings Limited. The latter's PSC page could not be opened. Their precise intermediate equity relationship is therefore omitted; the Austrian regulator directly supports Smith's indirect control.
Exor's opened ownership disclosure is dated 2025-12-31. Searches for subsequent ownership changes did not establish a newer controlling-shareholder observation.
Other Economist holdings, treasury shares and share-class denominators were not fully reconciled. The graph does not allocate an inferred residual percentage.

The Economist Group and its reporting parent The Economist Newspaper Limited are represented together to avoid inventing a parent-subsidiary layer. Giovanni Agnelli B.V. reaches the three-level tracing limit.
Trustees are represented collectively. Their reserved powers do not establish economic ownership or an independence assessment.
